Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB249.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fangrongxi. Fangrong Ruxi owns the retained deployment: the whole earth is the Zhaozhou pass, and the three kinds of self-deceivers exhaust their tricks.

Senses.Explanation: The pass named for the old master himself, where the school sets its barrier: his own Stone Bridge gate, the clouds that lock it, and the ruling that the whole earth is the crossing. Zhaozhou Congshen, meeting a monk fresh from the south, asks whether he knows the Zhaozhou pass — the monk claims to, and is called a salt-smuggler; the pass is hard to cross, and asked what it is, the master answers: the Stone Bridge; Yuanwu Keqin, entering Jiashan, verses that all things round themselves out and calls for anyone who has got through the Zhaozhou pass to step out — and when asked what the Jiashan pass is, backs off three hundred paces; Guxue Zhenzhe, at the kasaya presentation, rules the Sword-Pavilion road is dangerous but crossable — the Zhaozhou pass is truly hard to walk; and Fangrong Ruxi, sweeping the founding teacher's stupa, widens the image: the whole earth is the Zhaozhou pass, and three kinds of people — those who claim entry, claim exit, claim free passage — exhaust their tricks with no escape left. Sanyi Mingyu, at the rain prayer, verses that clouds lock the Zhaozhou pass and rain beats the Yunmen universal, yet lifting one hair-tip, no mote of scorched earth in any land; Tian'an Sheng, staff in hand at the autumn turn, lets the clouds leave the Zhaozhou pass and bore east and west at will while autumn enters the Yunmen universal, seven-free and eight-across; Dahui Zonggao, raising the cypress-tree case anew for Li Hanlao — verses that breaking through the Zhaozhou pass he still hunts for words, since at first he only spoke of the thatch's length and only when it burned knew the ground was uneven — is preserved by Yingshan Zhiyin's raised-old commentary; and Zhuanyu Guanheng, on his first visit to Yunju, asks how many have crossed the Zhaozhou pass — blue streams shut the dust far off, moonlight on the lake idle from of old.
